definition: Standard deviation is the square root of variance, restoring the original units of the data; in finance this same quantity is called volatility, and in science/engineering it is called root mean square (RMS).
core_idea: Standard deviation is the most commonly used dispersion measure precisely because taking the square root of variance converts squared units (e.g., dollars-squared) back into the original, interpretable units (e.g., dollars), and it is the specific quantity traders mean when they discuss market volatility.
key_points: Standard deviation = square root of variance; denoted lowercase sigma (s).
Same underlying quantity has different names by field: standard deviation (general statistics), root mean square/RMS (science/engineering), volatility (finance/trading).
Standard deviation is highlighted as the key concept traders reference when discussing market volatility.
relationships: Directly derived from variance by square root; variance itself is the average squared deviation from the mean.
trading_implications: 'Volatility' as traders use the term is mathematically the standard deviation of a price/return series, not a vague qualitative notion.
caveats: Treating volatility as a separate concept from standard deviation rather than recognizing it as the same statistical quantity under a different name in finance.
